scope: Static IL review of the original SESU 3.0.7 package download path; no original code was executed, no vendor host was contacted and nothing was installed

method.disassembler: ikdasm.exe from owned Mono 6.12.0 (sha256 696dfe5544d38343175c0dbce1ec9f6b823cf1309e1dfd4ad2b73e6ca57841d3) under mono-sgen64 (sha256 91b99fc4b1158785b43506f2d76f9998c31f0492128e5789fbaaab0e300afd49); monodis64 from the same package for RVAs
method.string_decoder: research/decode_sesu_download_brick.py (static XOR index^170 table, pinned slices); all 107 obfuscated string accessors were resolved in the private annotated listing
method.method_text_sha256_note: Per-method hashes are of the exact ikdasm method block bytes (from '.method' to 'end of method') in the private listing

original_methods.method: DownloadChannel delete destination after integrity failure

url_source.observation: The URI passed to StartDownload is a MultiPlatformUpdate field (DownloadAddress) set from the selected catalogue file; StartDownload requires an absolute URI. SESU overrides IsUriOnSesuProductionHostUnSafe to false, so the production-host rule requiring a detached .signature is bypassed while MustCheckSignatureAfterDownload is false. A proxy credential, when present, is sent as request Credentials.

tls_and_certificates.observation: The constructor ORs Tls12 (0xC00) into the process-wide ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol. No ServerCertificateValidationCallback or ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback member is referenced by any retained SESU assembly, so .NET Framework default certificate and hostname validation is expected. No certificate pinning or explicit revocation-check setting was found.

redirects.observation: HttpWebRequest.AllowAutoRedirect is never set, so the .NET Framework default (follow, including to another host) applies. Exact scheme-downgrade and hop-limit behavior was not observed.

preflight_request.observation: StartDownload performs a full GetResponse on the URI and closes it before the worker starts, only to read Content-Disposition. The final file name is Path.GetFileName(uri.LocalPath) unless Content-Disposition supplies a UrlDecode'd name, whose invalid file-name characters are replaced by '_'. The destination is Path.Combine(callerDirectory, name); the directory is created if missing.

existing_file.observation: SESU sets HowToReactOnExistingFile=OverrideOnSizeOrTimeConflict. If the destination exists and a remote info request reports the same length and Last-Modified as the local file, no download occurs and the file is marked ready without running IntegrityCheck in DownloadChannel. Otherwise an existing destination is deleted before writing.

resume_and_partial.observation: Bytes are written to destination + '.partial'. A partial larger than Content-Length, or older than the server Last-Modified, is deleted. A smaller partial is resumed with a second request carrying AddRange(offset) and opened with FileMode.Append; the 206 status and Content-Range are not checked in these methods. After a failed transfer the partial is retained and re-dated to the server Last-Modified for a later resume.

size_bound.observation: Negative Content-Length is rejected. The total size is the server Content-Length, not the catalogue size. The copy loop ends when Read returns zero or a stop is requested; the byte count is not compared with Content-Length before success is reported. Whether a premature close throws or returns zero in .NET Framework was not observed.

verification_order.observation: The partial is first renamed over the destination (deleting any existing file) and re-dated; only then, if the SecurityType dictionary is nonempty, IntegrityCheck(destination) runs. It applies only entries whose dictionary key equals the destination directory name; SESU keys the dictionary by node ID and merges the first value per security type across all files in the node. Computed values are Blake2b, SHA-1, SHA-256 and the embedded Authenticode signer name/thumbprint from X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile (no chain validation in this method); comparison is trimmed and case-insensitive. A mismatch deletes the destination file. No file size is compared. When a flag set from its StartDownload argument is true, SESU's finished handler repeats IntegrityCheck on LastTriedDownloadPath and calls a further unresolved step only if it passes.

failure_handling.observation: Exceptions are caught and stored as ExceptionCaughtDuringLastDownload; the worker raises FinishedEvent. The only automatic retry is up to ten repeats after a detected hibernate/resume. Integrity exceptions become DownloadFileHasFailedIntegrityCheckException. There is no retained failure record other than logs and the .partial file.

cli_policy_differences: URL must be the https URL of one explicitly selected file in an exact raw response that reproduces a complete catalogue report; no Content-Disposition naming, no automatic file selection
TLS 1.2 minimum with system trust or only an explicit CA file; certificate and hostname verification cannot be disabled
Same-origin redirects only (at most five); cross-origin and scheme changes are refused
Declared catalogue size is a hard bound; Content-Length must equal it; truncation and oversize fail
SHA-1 and size are verified before publication, and a fresh update-package-file re-read must reproduce them
New exclusive temporary file; no resume; existing outputs are never overwritten or deleted
Failed bytes are retained as *.failed.partial with a *.failed.json record instead of deletion
No Authenticode, Blake2b or SHA-256 catalogue entries are evaluated; no execution or installation
unresolved: Runtime .NET Framework certificate, redirect, proxy and premature-close behavior of the original download
The SESU UI caller's destination directory and the meaning of the StartDownload install flag
Whether the original ever receives catalogue security types other than sha1 (the captured catalogue has only sha1)
Original installer launch, elevation, exit-code interpretation, restart and post-install recovery (Windows evidence required)
acceptance_limit: Static review only. It establishes what the retained IL does on the reviewed paths, not observed original download, integrity, installation or restart outcomes.
